Local police and the FBI continued searching for the suspect vehicle, prepared for a confrontation with desperate criminals.

At 9:30 am on the morning of January 30, 1997, Richmond, VA police respond to a report of shots fired at a local bank.  Two masked men brandishing automatic weapons confront, and open fire on officers responding to the call.  The gunmen exit the bank, and retreat on foot, eventually eluding the officers.  The FBI soon responds, only to find one bank teller dead, another wounded, and the bank's security guard shot four times, yet still alive.

In August 1992, a man returned to his Memphis home and discovered that his wife was missing.  The husband, as well as his friends, family and neighbors began to receive ransom calls.  FBI agents noticed that one neighbor seemed to have the best rapport with the kidnapper.  They began to question his level of involvement, but had to proceed carefully, knowing that he could be their only link to the missing woman.

In 1990 and 1991, Chicago police and the FBI were on the trail of a bank robber whose holdups were becoming increasingly violent.  The criminal consistently used stolen Japanese cars to carry out the robberies, so authorities hoped to identify him by tracking vehicle thefts.  When they finally located the man known as the bearded bandit, they learned that he did not work alone and he had made a pact never to surrender.

In 1988, new light was shed on the mysterious death of a South Carolina farmer when a criminal confessed that two prominent community members hired him to commit murder.  Local police and FBI agents arrested a wealthy businessman and later learned that, even behind bars, he commanded the power to corrupt and kill.  Using prison informants, agents had to prevent him from murdering again.

In October 1993, a robber surprised unsuspecting customers by dropping through the roof of a California bank.  When police arrived, he escaped from the roof in a hail of bullets.  A tip from a local resident led police and FBI agents to the perpetrator.  They would soon learn that he had masterminded a local kidnapping, and held the fate of an innocent woman in his hands.

Amid the cocaine wars of early 1980's Miami, three dead bodies led a multi-agency tactical squad to suspect that a group of cops might be involved in illegal drug busts.   Investigating rumors of corruption, the squad uncovered a ring of patrolmen who were making millions by ripping off smuggled cocaine.  The investigators set out to prove that even with the advantages wealth and the protection of a police badge, nobody is above the law.

In rural Texas, 13-year-old is kidnapped on her way to school.  Frantic to find her safely, her millionaire father calls local authorities and the FBI.  As police officers and agents conduct aerial surveillance, the father drives hundreds of miles through the night to deliver the ransom cash to a drop that the kidnappers keep changing.  In a final effort to save the young girl, investigators must engage in a dangerous firefight with five desperate criminals.

In November of 1994, when a Wells Fargo armored van disappeared from a Glendale, Arizona mall, local authorities and the FBI scrambled to recover it, and its cargo of nearly a million dollars. Six hours later, agents found the van, its driver shot dead inside and the money gone. It was a perfect hit by professionals who left no clue behind. Months passed before a solid lead developed. In January, a tip led agents to look into a former prison guard.

In New York, the FBI and local police join forces to battle the constant influx of Colombian cocaine into the city's ports.  One detective goes undercover, posing as a Mafia wise-guy, and infiltrates a drug gang connected to Pablo Escobar's Medellin cartel.  The detective must be bold, but cautious, taking on the role of a tough-guy, but always aware that if the gang suspects anything, they won't hesitate to kill him.

In Puerto Rico, the death of a government witness, and the suspicious circumstances surrounding it, lead the FBI and local authorities to suspect corruption in the highest levels of the police force. With the help of a cooperating witness, investigators find the scope of the corruption is far greater that they first thought. Authorities struggle to capture the rouge officers, men who once swore to uphold the law, but now use their power to commit heinous crimes.

California Highway Patrolman George Gwaltney discovered the body of 23-year-old Robin Bishop near her car on a remote desert highway.  Although he proclaimed his innocence the FBI lab experts were able to link tool marks found on the frame with tools found in Gwaltney's home.  Through the match of hairs and fibers and a unique test for detecting and identifying sperm, Gwaltney was placed at the scene of the crime.

A man is found suffocated in his Pennsylvania home, his checkbook, credit cards and vehicle appear to have been stolen.  Fingerprints from the victim identify a recent escapee from a minimum-security prison, as well as his girlfriend.  Investigators flag the dead man's credit cards, and are alerted when one is used in North Dakota.  The FBI is called in and joins another task force already assembled because of a suspected kidnapping.

In Wisconsin, a varsity athlete is blindfolded, gagged, and shoved into a van by four gunmen.  The kidnappers contact the victim's family and demand $30,000, but offer no instructions on how to transfer the money.  The victim's family contacts the police.  The boy's captors tell his family they have shot him, and will kill him if they do not receive their money.  At an agreed upon drop site, FBI agents approach the captor's vehicle, only to watch them flee and quickly be followed by authorities.

In 1991, the Safe Streets Task Force, a joint FBI / Washington D.C. Metropolitan Police Department organization, begins conducting an investigation into the violent activities of a local gang called the K Street Crew.  Gang members are suspected of involvement in several area homicides.  The FBI approaches several witnesses, hoping to convince them to testify against the gang members.  Seven potential witnesses are murdered during the course of the investigation.

In June of 2000, two gunmen rob a Seattle, WA bank, and flee on foot as officers chase them.  One of the gunmen is killed in a firefight with police, the other escapes after assaulting a family and using their home to hide.  The family helps FBI agents identify the man, who is suspected of several other robberies.  Seattle SWAT teams, working with the FBI, search the home of the assailant's mother, and find ammunition matching that used at the bank robbery.

A California bank manager panics and calls in the FBI after the door to his vault refuses to open.  Upon inspection, the vault has been blasted into from the ceiling, and over $2 million in valuables is gone.  When agents find no clues as to the robbers or their whereabouts in California, they send details of the crime to other FBI field offices.  It is not long before agents in Ohio are investigating a bank vault robbery that is strikingly similar to the California heist.

Ando is struggling with the fact that his friend Shishigami is responsible for the spree of home invasions. After reading that hospital patients were being cured, Ando theorizes that there is someone else out there with the same powers as Shishigami. Ando lures Inuyashiki by pretending to need help and asks him to stop Shishigami. Meanwhile, Shishigami learns his mother has terminal cancer.

Shishigami escaped from a dozen officers, but he has become a wanted man in connection to the home invasion spree. With nowhere to go, Shishigami stays with Shion Watanabe, a classmate who has feelings for him. Meanwhile, Inuyashiki learns to use his robot abilities with Ando's help. After seeing Shishigami's mother publicly apologizing on TV, they worry what Shishigami might do next.

As Shion believed he was innocent, Shishigami confesses to her that his body is a robot and has taken many lives in order to feel alive again. He coldly informs her that he will kill everyone in the country. However, Shion begs Shishigami not to leave her behind. Shion cries as she tells Shishigami that the people he's killed had futures and loved ones, and Shishigami makes a proposition.

Kid has a new phantom thief rival in town, who flew all the way from France: Chat Noir! The felonious feline challenges Kid to steal a cat's-eye ring which may have belonged to Marie Antoinette, but this time, tough security measures have also been imported from France.

The Elrics discover the horrific ingredient needed to create a Philosopher's Stone. When night falls, they prowl the grounds of a secret laboratory in search of more facts - but the brothers find only danger.
Ed and Al furiously battle the Fifth Laboratory's psychotic guards. In the chaos, the truth behind the Philosopher's Stone is buried beneath rubble - and disturbing new questions are unearthed.

Al is haunted by the notion his entire existence was simply created by his brother. When the youngest Elric angrily reveals these suspicions, only Winry can convince him just how wrong he is about Ed.

programmes.d: Naruto, Sakura, and Kakashi team up with Rock Lee to escort Prince Michiru and his son Hikaru, but a villainous uprising awaits their homecoming.

Dr. Eggman reveals to Sonic that he had been double-crossed by Chaos. As Knuckles warns Sonic of dangers of Chaos if he was to obtain the last Chaos Emerald, they are transported to the past by a mysterious red orb.
As he hacks GUN's computer database, Dr. Eggman discovers his grandfather's mysterious "Ultimate Life Form" project named Shadow.
Sonic is accused of causing havoc in Prison Island. As GUN agents seek after Sonic, Sonic attempts to figure out who had framed him.

A Count challenges Lupin to steal a gemstone named Dracula's Tear from on board his airship, the Hendenburg. However, also on board the Hendenburg are several formidable detectives: Sherlock Holmes III, Philip Archer, Kosuke Kindani and Inspector Zenigata. Will Lupin accept the Count's challenge and will he be able to complete the task before the airship lands, where the police will be waiting for him?

Lupin is suffering from Transformation Sickness, an illness that transforms him into a cruel, cold-blooded criminal at the stroke of midnight, and leaves him with no recollection of his murderous crime spree in the morning. In despair, Lupin even contemplates taking his own life, but is the "other Lupin" really Lupin?

Oga hears about the legendary Tojo, the final and strongest member of Ishiyama's TKKH, from Furuichi. And right away, he goes for a showdown! Well, if he knew where Tojo was. Thanks to Himekawa's digging, Oga, Hilda, and the rest head to the beach where Tojo is supposed to be working part-time...

Their work done, Doctor Furcas and Lamia head back to the Demon World, but Oga, Beel, and Furuichi accidentally hitch along for the ride! With Alaindelon out of commission after exceeding his maximum interdimensional transfer weight limit, the gang has no choice but to search for his daughter, but they have to make it through Vlad's Haunt in one piece first!

In search of Alaindelon's daughter so they can get back home, Oga and the gang head to a city of criminal Demon Beast poachers to rescue her. But before they get the chance, a giant monster appears to take revenge on the poachers for the harm they've done to Vlad's Haunt. And the only one who can stand toe-to-toe with it is... Baby Beel?!

The family of 19-year-old Jake Limberios continues to search for answers surrounding his death in March 2012. Who fired the gunshot that ended his life? Brittany and Will, who witnessed the shooting, say Jake, a gun enthusiast, accidentally shot himself in the head. Although the coroner ruled his death a suicide, Jake’s parents, Mike and Shannon, say their son, a young father, never would’ve taken his own life. Left with so many unanswered questions, Jake’s parents had his body exhumed and autop
The conversation continues with Heather, who says she is not at fault for her son's accidental overdose. But- where was she that night?

Dr. Phil follows up with a family whose story captivated viewers. Fourteen siblings say they suffered horrific beatings and molestation at the hands of their own father, who claimed to be the Messiah. The oldest daughter, Jeanne, says she was not only abused by her dad, but was forced to brutally beat her younger brothers and sisters to please their controlling patriarch. After the show, the relatives say they made great strides toward reconciliation, but tension and resentment still exist. Miri

The new series Dahmer - Monster: The Jeffrey Dahmer Story may have landed the number one spot on Netflix, but it wasn’t popular with everyone. Angry family members of Dahmer’s victims say the controversial drama re-traumatized them and romanticized the notorious serial killer. You’ve seen Hollywood’s version. Dr. Phil continues his series on how to survive inflation. Today, financial experts share money-saving and money-making tips to help you learn how to take control of your finances during inflation. Plus, find out the best ways to use money to make money, savings hacks, freebie secrets, and get advice on how to set up the next generation for financial success.

Frankie and his former wife, Karen Leanne Dees, made headlines and were the subject of a Lifetime movie called Baby Brokers. The couple was accused of scamming would-be parents out of thousands of dollars by promising them one of their unborn babies in exchange for financial support. Frankie says he and Karen had 10 children, and he claims eight of those children were placed for adoption without his knowledge. His daughters Sandy and Ava claim their biological father not only knew about the adop

How has the role of the man evolved in the modern family? One woman claims her husband provides her with everything—except love and affection. He says he only knows how to provide financially. Can Dr. Phil help them find a balance and save their marriage of 17 years? Then, one guest entered into a new relationship after leaving his wife and kids. Now, his guilt is causing him to lie, manipulate and become physically abusive. Find out what Dr. Phil has to say to these men about the true measure o

Two families desperate to find their missing children ask Dr. Phil for help. Two-year-old Bianca disappeared while in the care of her father. He says she was taken when he was carjacked. Was he involved in her disappearance? And, Josh hasn’t seen his son, Trenton, since he was 2 years old, more than five years ago. Did the boy's mother, who died by suicide, take clues with her to the grave?

Just one day off heroin, Sarah is monitored medically as she goes through painful withdrawal symptoms. Tecoa has been clean for two weeks, but struggles with her own drug cravings while six months pregnant and providing support for her detoxing sibling. Is she sabotaging Dr. Phil's efforts to get Sarah healthy? Dr. Phil shows Sarah and Tecoa a terrifying look into their future. Is it enough to scare them straight?

Are you living way beyond your means? Do you shop for one pair of shoes, but come home with 10? Do you look great on the outside, while secretly facing financial ruin? Dr. Phil has advice for putting down the checkbook.
The case of Thomas Cogdell, who confessed to his sister's muder at age 12, is examined.

Dr. Phil delves into a tragic story that spanned several decades, shattered lives and left one person behind bars. Fourteen children were held captive by a man who called himself The Messiah … a man who was also their father. Jeanne says she was raised in this environment, which the authorities called cult-like, and that she and her siblings were starved, beaten and had no schooling. In a tear-jerking revelation, Jeanne tells Dr. Phil that she was forced to perform unthinkable sexual acts with h

Despite having 3,000 bottles of shampoo, 30,000 shirts, 5,000 cookbooks, and boxes on top of boxes of things, Kristen says she doesn’t think she is a hoarder. But Kristen claims her “collection of things” has created a problem. She just bought a new house and after already moving in 600 boxes, she says she's completely running out of room, and there is a whole lot more to pack. Tara had big dreams when she married Steve. Now, she feels like she's signed on to a life of misery and a mother-in-law who butts into their business.

When 24-year-old Andee last met with Dr. Phil, she was struggling with drug addiction -- and her parents, Pam and Ed, blamed each other. After the taping, Andee says she completed 90 days of rehab but later relapsed and is now worse than ever. Is she finally ready to commit to staying clean?

Anthony says he fears his 29-year-old brother, Jamie, a fitness model and personal trainer, won’t live to see 30 if he doesn’t get serious help with his addictions. Anthony says Jamie has struggled for years with cocaine, alcohol and anger issues -- all of which he says are exacerbated by their “enabling” parents, Steve and Joey. Two moms ask Dr. Phil to give their sons a reality check. Rita says her son, Eric, changed his name to “King Keith” and is forgoing a college education to pursue a singing career. Has he lost touch with reality? And, Cheryl says her college-educated son, Patrick, is lazy and lacks ambition.

Dr. Phil meets guests who say their perfect day was ruined by everything from booze, to broken down limousines, to grooms from hell, and now their marriages suffer because they can't stop reliving their wedding gone bad.

She’s been engaged four times but says she gets cold feet before she makes it down the aisle. Rick, her current fiancé, proposed four years ago and is still waiting for her to set a wedding date. Now, they’re worried this could lead to a life of crime. Plus, a boy whose nickname is Dracula because he’s always biting somebody! The saga of a father's quest for his vanished daughter is discussed.

They’re self-absorbed, spoiled and entitled brats, otherwise known as Generation Me. MTV correspondent Kim Stolz recently hit the streets of New York to find out how the younger generation feels about this label. Don't miss the candid responses. Then, Bradley, 24, says he wants to be rich and drive a Lamborghini, but he only wants to put in 80 percent of the effort. He still relies on his mom, Christine, to pay his rent and other bills. Will Bradley learn to stand on his own two feet? Plus, Moni

The 1957 kidnapping and murder of Maria Ridulph went cold for 55 years, until Jack McCullough, once known as John Tessier, was arrested and eventually convicted -- despite maintaining his innocence. Dr. Phil speaks to family members on both sides. Could McCullough have been wrongfully convicted?
Domestic battles are never fun. But what happens when battling becomes a lifestyle? Today's guests want to learn how to put an end to their family feud once and for all.

Her parents and several therapists have failed to help her erase her distorted body image. This 19-year-old battles both anorexia and bulimia. With the help of her parents, fiancé, and brother, Dr. Phil discusses the steps to recovery. Plus, meet another young woman who lives alone with her disease and her sense of complete failure. Dr. Phil explains early detection, the warning signs, and treatment.

In a headline-grabbing case, 22-year-old Sheena Morris was found hanged in a Florida hotel room on New Year's Day 2009, just hours after reports of an altercation between Sheena and her fiancé, Joe, now 48. Her death was ruled a suicide, but Sheena's parents refuse to believe that their daughter would take her own life -- they feel she was murdered, and that Joe may be responsible. Dr. Phil’s son, Jay, was working with a family for his new reality show when the mom, Vikki, phoned to say that her son, Justin, had been using drugs. Learn how one single mother’s yelling and offensive language are driving away her teenage kids. Plus, one woman gave up a career to be a stay-at-home mom. Jamie’s brother, Anthony, says their parents have enabled Jamie at every turn -- including failing to acknowledge Jamie’s other serious problem, which he refuses to discuss. After storming off stage, Jamie rejoins the conversation. Is he ready to be completely honest with his family -- and with himself? Dr. Phil has a sobering wake-up call for Jamie -- and for hi
Have you ever felt like you had to walk on eggshells around someone, constantly worrying about how they would react to anything you said or did? What if you were married to that person?

Is it asking too much for your 20-something child to make his or her own money and live independently? Barbara says her daughter, Chelsea, needs to grow up! She says she’s given her daughter nothing but the best, and all she has to show for it is a lying child who won’t speak to her. Chelsea says she can’t live up to her mom’s “rich bitch” expectations and just wants to be left alone. Mother and daughter see each other on the Dr. Phil stage for the first time in seven months, and sparks fly! Is
Dr. Phil speaks with some opinionated guests! Can he get them to see that their opinions and judgments can be hurtful?

Criminals, deadbeats and bad boys -- most women run from these types of men, but some women say Mr. Wrong is the right guy for them. Kelly says her daughter, Heather, married Mr. Wrong, and the price she paid was losing her children. Kelly says Heather's husband, Earl, is an unfit father and can't provide for the family. Heather, 25, says she stands by her 41-year-old husband, and wants her parents to stop sabotaging her marriage. Are Heather and Earl really unfit parents, or does Earl deserve a

Witness the “boomerang effect...” Dr. Phil talks to parents whose adult children keep coming back to live with, and off of them. One couple says their sons refuse to move out even though they are both almost 30-years-old. One 25- year-old is unemployed, has had 16 jobs in seven years, lives with his mother and even took her credits cards to charge up two thousand dollars worth of “stuff.” Dr. Phil helps these adult children address their issues so they can stop their destructive patterns.

After a Tennessee mother caused an international uproar when she sent her 7-year-old adopted son on a one-way flight back to Russia, the subject of international adoptions is making front-page headlines. Dr. Phil speaks with moms who say they relate to the Tennessee woman, and unless you walk a mile in their shoes, you have no way of understanding. Jane says she had no idea her 2-year-old daughter, Mikhaela, was profoundly deaf and autistic when she adopted her from the Ukraine eight years ago.

The last day in The House approaches as the four couples are put to one more test. To examine how each couple contaminates their relationship with unrealistic expectations, Dr. Phil gives one person from each pair a ""bump in the road."" Donning a pregnancy suit, Lacey surprises Kalin with the news that she's pregnant with someone else's child. Kalin tells her that he would leave her. Steve is made to look older and obese. Not surprisingly, Stephanie tells him that she would take control of his

Daniel Pelosi was convicted of second-degree murder in the slaying of investment banker and multimillionaire Ted Ammon -- the husband of his lover, Generosa. He is currently serving 25 years to life but now claims he is ready to explain what really happened the night of the murder. Dr. Phil visits Pelosi behind bars.

Paul was his family’s rock and role model, so when he suddenly passed away, his wife and four children say their lives were shattered. Debbie, who was married to Paul for 30 years, says she shut down after his death and doesn’t know how to unite her brood. Sisters Jamie, Erica and Tayler say they don’t know how to properly grieve, they’re always fighting with each other, and they’re upset that their brother, Paul, turned his back on them. Paul says he didn’t run away from his loved ones; he has
A stay-at-home mother says she can't control her rage, and she takes it out on her kids. Dr. Phil intervenes for the sake of her five precious children.

Can a mistress save a marriage? Chrissy fears that she’ll have to embrace this drastic option to salvage her relationship. Her husband, Scott, has been having an affair with Tracy for five years, and he wants Chrissy to consider negotiated infidelity, an arrangement where partners are given permission to stray. He even suggested that his mistress buy the house next door to theirs! Chrissy says Scott is a loving dad to their three kids, and she wonders if there’s hope for their 10-year marriage.

Have you ever been so devastated after a breakup that you wanted someone to literally pay for your broken heart? Or, have you ever wanted to exact revenge on someone who you believe stole a lover away from you? Dr. Phil's guests are broken-hearted lovers entangled in nasty lawsuits.

Parent alert: If you have a teenager, watch this show with him or her. Dr. Phil takes a close look at the harsh reality of young girls and boys having a baby while they're still just a baby themselves. It doesn't just happen to the bad girl down the street; your child can become pregnant while living under your roof.
Some moms don't want to grow up, and others don't want to grow old. Dr. Phil talks to women walking on the wild side and tries to rein them back in!

What do you do when life’s problems seem so overwhelming that it feels like there’s no way out? Kenny, who was one of the first responders to the 9/11 tragedy, says he still struggles with post-traumatic stress disorder and other health challenges. His wife, Cyndi, and daughter, Gina, say he just sits on the couch and obsesses about that fateful day, and they feel he needs to get over it. Can Kenny get his life and his health back? Then, Steve and Jacki have been married for four years, and Stev

Michael is a “starving artist” who thinks getting a 9 to 5 job would interfere with his creativity. He’s broke, jobless and was recently homeless and living in the woods. His mother, Pat, wants him to get a real job, stop being a mooch, and start being more like his professional brothers! Then, meet two brothers: one has an MBA and a successful career, while the other has been addicted to drugs and running from the police. His parents are worried he may end up in prison for the rest of his life.

Every 10 seconds an animal is abused in this country. By the time this show is over, nearly 240 animals will be tortured. Dr. Phil, a huge animal lover, is taking a stand. First up, Rob says dog fighting is not a crime, and believes that it’s no different than boxing or football. He was convicted of a felony after authorities caught him in the act and says he wants to clear up the misconception about dog fighting. Is this “sport” in Rob’s DNA, or can he be rehabilitated? Will Rob get a wake-up c

When Sheena Morris was found hanged in a Florida hotel room on New Year's Day 2009, her death was ruled a suicide. But the 22-year-old's parents, Kelly and David, say they believe their daughter was murdered, and have since been working relentlessly to reopen the investigation into her death, which is now under review. On Dr. Phil's stage, they come face to face with the man they believe killed Sheena -- her 48-year-old fiancé, Joe. Were there clues missed in the original investigation? Then, Jo

Former high school dance teacher Anne, 35, made national headlines when it was revealed that her two children -- ages 3 and 2 -- were fathered by Bradman, a former student who is 14 years her junior. Bradman, now 21, is claiming that their physical relationship began when he was 15 and that Anne made the first move. In part two of “Profiles of a Pregnancy,” Dr. Phil tackles common decisions couples face during the 40-week roller coaster ride of pregnancy. One father-to-be refuses to be in the delivery room when his wife goes into labor; but she wants him by her side. Will this squeamish husband take Dr. Phil’s advice or will he opt for the waiting room? Then, Dr. Phil checks back with new parents-to-be Shannon and Morgan to see how they’re progressing. Plus, Robin surprises the couple with a brand new nurse

Sarah and Tecoa's mother, Cindy, sits down with Dr. Phil to answer some hard questions about how her daughters' lives have spun so out of control. Dr. Phil shows her some of the video footage of Sarah's life on the street, selling her body, smoking crack cocaine and shooting heroin, while Tecoa explains how it all began. In a race against time, Dr. Phil gets the sisters off the streets and into The Dr. Phil House. Will Sarah and Tecoa commit to rehab and stay clean?

Lance discovers a massive hive under the roof of a Palm Springs artist who donates the proceeds of her work to environmental causes; he uncovers a swarm in an unlikely place by a swimming pool.
Lance visits a neighbor who has a lot of cats; the team extracts a beehive that's under the ground; at the end of a hard day of work, Lance and crew take a road trip to visit a bee apiary.

programmes.d: Chuck visits Gesgapegiac, a Mi'kmaq community in East Quebec. Alongside Stephen Jerome, he fishes a beautiful river full of salmon, learns about basket-weaving, and cooks a traditional local recipe.
Culinary Travels has found some incredible flavors in Napa Valley, California. We will be sampling the region's famous wines before discovering fresh cuisine at two luxury resorts.
Professional Mixologist Jonas Ax reveals his depth of knowledge of all things shaken, stirred, chilled, and sparkling as host Phillip Davenport spends an afternoon at Elysium Bar and Terrace.
The Marina Bay Sand's Epicurean Market in Singapore is a culinary force.

Beginning in the exquisite fishing port of Bosa, Yotam prepares one of the Mediterranean's classic meals: freshly caught lobster on an open fire pit. Leaving the coast behind, he then travels into the rugged Sardinian heartland.

Welcome to Ganvie, land of the unsubdued, the free, the resistance, and of peaceful waters. In Ganvie, the Tofinu people live on the water. To do so they must move at a careful pace, learn to live without excess, and form deep bonds of family and friendship to survive.
Travel the country and discover the wackiest oddities it has to offer.

Experience the supreme and sacred spectacle of the Grand Canyon. This insider's view of one of the world's greatest natural wonders takes you rim-to-rim to hike hidden canyons, plunge into ancient pools, raft world-class rapids, discover manmade gems, and explore extreme backcountry.

programmes.t: Lonely Planet: Best Parks Ever - America's National Parks
programmes.d: Volcanoes erupt and geysers explode in this sizzling episode. Take a look at the hottest parks you can visit!

programmes.t: Moments in Time with Elia Locardi
programmes.d: Prague is as beautiful as it is historic, and it’s also one of the best cities in Europe for photography. After navigating the city streets to find the best photo spots, Elia gets a tour of Erik Johansson's photography studio.
Milwaukee with Denella Ri'chard.

In Denver, Colorado we meet with banjo virtuoso Bela Fleck, visit the workshop where the GRAMMY statuettes are lovingly handcrafted, and explore nearby ski resorts, local record stores, dance clubs to soak in the Denver experience.

This is your chance to experience the rich culture of Sicily. Music Voyager travels into the heart of Sicily where we will dine with royalty and toast the region's famous vineyards amid the shadows of Mount Etna.
Pamela visits the Cu Chi Tunnels and offers travel tips in Packing with Pamela.

In the Bronx, Mickela meets with the largest Garifuna community in the United States, a people of Afro-Caribbean culture with Central American influences whose dances and music have miraculously survived generations of incredible odds.

A delightful discussion over cake and tea leads Rosemary and Catherine into the kitchen where Rosemary reveals her recipe for Stout Soused Herrings, a recipe Catherine will take with her to recreate in Paris for Rosemary's daughter, Una.

In London, Mary Claire dreams of nettle and leek soup with homemade brown bread. With familial guidance on behalf of Sheila and Joe Kirwan in Clonegal, Catherine travels to London to surprise Mary Claire with a little taste of home.

programmes.t: My Greek Table with Diane Kochilas
programmes.d: Diane sets out for Paros to find a young visionary farmer named Alkis Downward and his fiancee who have been tilling the Downward family land for five years and have created a successful and sustainable agriculture production facility.

programmes.t: Mexico One Plate at a Time with Rick Bayless
programmes.d: Rick provides in-depth details on the preparation of a classic chiles rellenos.

programmes.t: Mexico One Plate at a Time with Rick Bayless
programmes.d: Chorizo is the "bacon of Mexico."

Jeremy's BBQ Chicken Wings with Spicy Slaw is sure to impress. Joe prepares a perfect Malaysian Fried Rice. After being inspired by Drunken Prawns in a home dedicated to whisky, Jeremy makes Cinnamon Bao Doughnuts and Chocolate Sauce.

Grab your winter gear and head to Quebec City where Colleen's family explores the Winter Carnival and the Hotel de Glace, rides down a mountain on a giant snow tube, tries their hand at dog sledding, and savors maple syrup goodies.

The grandest of canyons awaits! While in Northern Arizona, the Kellys also pay a visit to Bearizona to meet some of the region's wildlife, and take a real wild west train ride on the Grand Canyon Railway.

Isolated from geopolitics for the past 30 years, Laos is now slowly opening to tourism. Its cultures and environment are fragile, and a responsible form of tourism could preserve its past and character. From fishing villages to the forests of northern Laos, meet the people that protect their land.

Sri Lanka is principally known for its heavenly beaches, bold-green mountains and forests, its glorious waterfalls, and renowned tea plantations. It has begun to preserve its ecological resources, and respect the environment more and more, so that everyone may enjoy the land's bounty over time.

programmes.t: Lonely Planet: Best Parks Ever - America's National Parks
programmes.d: From the most scenic drive in America, to the world's largest bowl of fresh water, these parks have the wettest landscape for your pleasure.

Toronto is a bright, bustling cosmopolitan city whose residents have roots across the globe. You will find everything in Toronto, including world-class food, art, culture, beaches, museums, nightlife, theaters, and the beautiful outdoors.
Be tailgate-ready with these quesadillas, burgers and pork chops.
Experience Baltimore’s grilling traditions, from pit beef to local seafood.
The chefs cook their fish courses. Theyre all vying to finish in the top three and still be in with a chance of cooking at the special banquet.
Its judgement day as the chefs not only learn the top three desserts but the judges announce the winning menu. Fast show writer and performer Charlie Higson helps judge the puddings.

It's the climax of the competition as the winning chefs cook at the Comic Relief Banquet at the Royal Albert Hall. But its not plain sailing - the chefs have to contend with getting into the kitchen late.

Today three of Scotlands top chefs, Jak ODonnell, Jimmy Lee, and Graham Campbell attempt to impress this weeks veteran judge. Returning finalist Jak is determined to make it to the banquet, but newcomers Jimmy and Graham are out to steal her crown.

Today Scottish chefs, Jak ODonnell, Jimmy Lee and Graham Campbell fight it out for the fish course. Graham is in a confident mood but returning finalist Jak and Jimmy are pushing him hard. Will the pressure prove too much for ambitious Graham?

Today Scottish chefs Jak ODonnell, Jimmy Lee and Graham Campbell are battling to plate up a perfect main course for this weeks veteran chef. Self-taught Jimmy is honouring his Mum with his rendition of her Chinese Beef Stew.

Today its the Scottish chefs last chance to impress, with the dessert course. Only two can cook for the judges tomorrow, and with one chef in the lead after a triumphant main, the pressures on for the other two to plate up perfection.

Today the two remaining Scottish chefs cook their entire menus again for the judges Prue Leith, Oliver Peyton and Matthew Fort. Theyre joined by WI Calendar Girl Angela Baker, who will help decide which chef will go forward to the National Finals.
Today three of the South Wests finest chefs - Jude Kereama, Josh Eggleton and Dominic Chapman - attempt to impress this weeks veteran judge with their starters.

Today the three South West chefs - Jude Kereama, Josh Eggleton and Dominic Chapman fight it out for the fish course. Despite school-boy errors yesterday, experienced Dominic is determined to get a high score today.
Today its a battle for the main course with the three South West chefs - Jude Kereama, Josh Eggleton and Dominic Chapman going head to head.

Today its the last chance for the South Wests chefs to impress, with the dessert course. Only two chefs can go through to cook for the judges so with everything to play for, who will plate up perfection and who will be sent packing?

Today the two remaining South West chefs cook their entire menus again for the judges Prue Leith, Oliver Peyton and Matthew Fort. Joining the judges is Radhika Bynon, a member of the Forest Gate, Womens Institute, a modern urban group of women.
Today representing Wales Stephen Gomes, Adam Bannister and Phil Carmichael are challenged to plate up perfect starter courses for this weeks veteran judge.

Today the three Welsh chefs - Stephen Gomes, Adam Bannister and Phil Carmichael fight it out for the fish course. Experimental chef Stephen is determined to prove himself with a fish course honouring the WIs tradition of preserving.

Its a battle for the main course with the Welsh chefs - Stephen Gomes, Adam Bannister and Phil Carmichael are going head to head. With all 3 chefs paying homage to Welsh lamb; the pressure is on to deliver a main worthy of their veterans approval.

Today its the tricky dessert course, and the last chance for the Welsh chefs to secure their place in tomorrows regional final. Only two can make it through, and one will leave the competition for good.
Today the two remaining Welsh chefs cook their four courses again for the judges Prue Leith, Oliver Peyton and Matthew Fort along with guest judge and long serving WI member Rosemary Bishton.
Three of Northern Irelands top chefs Chris McGowan, Danni Barry and Ben Arnold go head to head with their starter courses to impress this weeks veteran judge.
Today three of Northern Irelands top chefs Chris McGowan, Danni Barry and Ben Arnold are cooking their fish courses. Ambitious Ben is determined to steal Chriss regional crown.
Today its a battle for the main course for three of Northern Irelands finest chefs Chris McGowan, Danni Barry and Ben Arnold. Ambitious Ben is out to prove himself with a perfect lamb main course.

Its dessert day and the Northern Irish chefs are all striving for one of the two spots in tomorrows Regional Final. The pressure is intense, and in the end one chef must leave the competition empty handed.
Today the two remaining North Irish chefs are cooking all four courses again for the judges Prue Leith, Oliver Peyton and Matthew Fort.

Three newcomers, Mini Patel, Michael OHare and Tim Allen are going head to head this week for a chance to represent the North East region in the National Finals. Today its a battle for starter course, and the first chance to impress their veteran chef.
Its the fight for the fish course, as three of the North Easts finest chefs Mini Patel, Michael OHare and Tim Allen are out to impress.

Today three of the North Easts most dynamic chefs - Mini Patel, Michael OHare and Tim Allen - go head to head cooking their main courses. Michelin starred Tim is super keen to bag the first ten of the week, but Michael and Mini are hot on his heels.

Its the North East chefs last chance to impress with the dessert course. Its been a week of highs and lows, modern audacious dishes and classic masterpieces but with only two places are up for grabs cooking for the judges.

Two remaining North East chefs must cook all four courses again for the judges Prue Leith, Oliver Peyton and Matthew Fort. Theyre joined by a guest judge who will help decide who will go through to represent the North East in the National Finals.

Representing the North West are Eve Townson, Matt Worswick and returning contender Mark Ellis. Todays the starter course, and after failing to cook for the judges last year Marks out to redeem himself.

Its the fish course, as three of the North Wests finest chefs Eve Townson, Matt Worswick and Mark Ellis go head to head. Eve and Matt are hoping their classic approach to cooking fish will win the day.

Ralph (Mary Grace Canfield) is distraught when her beloved Mr. Kimball, is fired as the county agricultural agent. Out of a job, Kimball (Alvy Moore) no longer has money enough to marry the lady-carpenter-in-waiting! But wait�did he even want to?

Lisa weaves the tale of her great, great grandmother, the Queen of the Gypsies, to explain a bizarre family tradition: a woman in her family must marry an American -- but only every fourth generation -- in order to gain a special inheritance.

After Oliver (Eddie Albert) accidentally drops a hammer on her head, Lisa (Eva Gabor) develops a case amnesia, with no idea who she is or why she is on a farm in Hooterville�and she adamantly refuses to believe that Oliver is her husband!

Nothing gets done on the Douglas farm when Oliver (Eddie Albert) gifts Eb (Tom Lester) a top-of-the-line radio for his birthday. Letting nothing stop him, Eb (Tom Lester) enters a radio contest...even when Eleanor the cow swallows the radio whole.

It's a very official third season premiere for Green Acres when the retirement of a state senator leaves Hooterville considering its best candidate for the job. Of course, they turn to their beloved lawyer-come-farmer Oliver Douglas (Eddie Albert).

Oliver finds himself in a jam after asking Lisa to make him homemade fruit preserves. An episode deliciously devoted to Lisa's culinary escapades, Lisa musters all of her Hungarian might to make Oliver the best peach jam he's ever tasted.

After years of substandard service, Oliver is hellbent on throwing the book at the Hooterville Phone Company. When it becomes clear that the local utility oversight board can't do much about it, he decides to handle matters directly.

Mr. Trendell, the president of the Hooterville Phone Company, hands the company over to a delighted Oliver. But after a day of crossed wires and a switchboard repairman with some lose connections of his own, Oliver is ready to call it quits.

For the first time, Oliver has a successful crop that needs picking. His tomatoes have grown beautifully. But matters at the phone company continue divide his precious time, so Oliver looks for an interested buyer to take the company off his hands.

Being president of the Hooterville Phone Company has been a rude awakening for Oliver. The switchboard operator is now calling him at five in the morning! After a bevy of new complaints from unhappy customers, Oliver has just about had enough.

One might think that when Eb takes a vacation things around the farm might go more smoothly. But when Eb elopes, leaving his cousin Walter to take his place, it turns out to be a horrible idea. Walter barely knows a weed from a hole in the ground!

Lisa is reminded that she stored a birthday present for Oliver years ago: a genuine Stavinsky. But what is it? It's a modern art sculpture that is two parts plumbing pipes, one part tire chains, and one part birdbath. Oliver calls it "The Thing."

The continually evolving story of how Lisa (Eva Gabor) and Oliver (Oliver) fell in love gets yet another version in this delightful episode. But one thing is for sure: Lisa and Oliver are just as in love today as the day when he fell out of the sky.

Green Acres is greener than ever, with jealousy. When Oliver (Eddie Albert) hires a handsome, young, intelligent Brit to take over his farm work while he is away, it doesn't take long for the newcomer to make a strong impression on Lisa (Eva Gabor).

Mr. Haney is up to his money-making schemes again. When a government representative tells Mr. Haney that the state is looking to purchase the Douglas farm for a new highway, Mr. Haney arranges to buy back the farm from the Douglases at a steal.

Ralph, the lady carpenter, runs away from home and stays with the Douglases after having a fight with her brother, Alf. While Oliver may never get his bedroom finished, he gains a maid as Ralph takes over as the Douglases' live-in housekeeper.

Picking apples while on a picnic, Oliver runs into the feisty Ira Hatch, the owner of the apple orchard. However, once back in town, Mr. Drucker tells Oliver that Hatch has been dead for years. An incredulous Oliver agrees to see a psychologist.

After his elopement and cross-country honeymoon, Eb returns to Hooterville. But his new wife is nowhere to be found! After sending postcards from all across the country, Eb has to confess that his fianc� stood him up at the alter on their big day.

Someone has stolen $300 from Mr. Drucker's general store, and it looks like Eb is the culprit. How else could he have bought himself a new car that cost, you guessed it, exactly $300? But that is just the first twist of the many turns of this story.

Lisa awakes, saying she's dreamt that she must invest in copper. When Oliver turns that idea down, she seizes on the opportunity to invest in a ten-year-old genius's electric company. Twenty-eight dollars buys her a third of the business.

Arnold, the Ziffels' television-loving pig, has taken on a paper route to save enough money for a new color set. But when bank robbers show up and threaten his dreams, and Lisa and Oliver are held captive in their own home, Arnold has to fight back.

The farmers of Hooterville are headed to France! Or at least they are if they can get organized. As part of an agricultural exchange program, the farmers are offered a chance to join a chartered government flight to Europe.

Lisa (Eva Gabor) is delighted to learn that her Hungarian mother is planning a visit to their little farm. Much to Oliver's (Eddie Albert) disbelief and dismay, a rumor spreads all around Hooterville that Lisa's mother is a European countess.

Love is in the air as the first day of spring arrives in Hooterville. And who better to lead the town in celebrating it than Lisa. She is resolved to show Oliver just what spring is all about and sets out to produce a Spring festival celebration.

It's a hair-raising episode as Eb (Tom Lester) enrolls in a correspondence course to become a barber. Lisa (Eva Gabor) and Oliver (Eddie Albert) give him the money to learn the trade but learning how to cut hair by mail has its glitches.

For a lawyer, Oliver should be more careful about what he signs. Lisa reminds him that two years ago Oliver made her a promise to take her back to New York for a two-week vacation. And she has it in writing� on the bottom of the kitchen drawer.

It's hard to know who has a curse over Oliver, but he sure has his hands full with Lisa and her fellow Hungarian Lazlo Broslav. Lazlo appears with a letter claiming he once saved the life of Lisa's uncle, and now her family must repay the debt.

There's a problem in Hooterville: no farmer seems able to grow a cash crop on account of the quality of the soil. But as it turns out from Oliver's (Eddie Albert) soil and mineral research, the oft misunderstood rutabaga is an ideal choice.

Green Acres goes Hollywood in this first installment of a two-part season finale. When Arnold the pig appears in a play at the Hooterville Theater, Lisa (Eva Gabor) arranges for an old friend to give Arnold a chance on the big screen.

It's a swine-sational third season finale for Green Acres, as Oliver and Lisa chaperone Arnold, the Ziffel's talented pig, to Hollywood for his big screen test. There's only one problem, Lisa failed to mention that Arnold is not your normal actor.

Hooterville is abuzz as the townsfolk enter a contest sponsored by Peterson's Poi Juice, with a trip to Hawaii as the top prize. But no one expects the winner to be Arnold, the Ziffels' talented pig. Maybe a pig might fly after all, to the islands!

A charity rummage sale asks for donated clothing. Being among the wealthier residents of Hooterville, the organizers look to the Douglases. It isn't long before Oliver has to stop Lisa from giving away his entire wardrobe!

Love is in the air when Eb is quickly engaged to Loreli Appleby, whom he has only known for a day. Eb tries to impress Loreli's father, a farmer, but in typical fashion, he accidentally ruins his future father-in-law's cabbage crop.

When Fire Chief Joe Carson is looking for a way to go to Miami, he hires Oliver as his assistant, hoping Oliver will pay for the trip. The plan backfires, no pun intended, when Oliver starts pointing out what a poor job the chief has been doing.

The highways in Hooterville are in dire need of repair. Oliver is fed up and believes he can make a difference by complaining to his state representative, Ben Hanks. But Hanks' popularity proves greater than his sense of responsibility.

Lisa feels like she should be contributing more and wants to start working in Oliver's construction business. Lisa is like a fish out of water as she arrives to the Monroes' workshop in overalls and causes one problem after another.

Lisa plays bovine matchmaker when Oliver and Lisa decide it is time for their female cow, Eleanor, to start providing milk for the farm. Oliver makes arrangements for Eleanor to mooooove in with the neighbor's bull, but Lisa has other ideas.

The townsfolk look forward to "Old Mail Day", when once a year undelivered mail is handed out. The delayed mail includes a letter all the way from 1917! Oliver is upset by the poor service, but his complaints land with more impact than he intended.

When word spreads that an agricultural student is coming to Hooterville to study with county agent Hank Kimball, no one seems to be interested. However, things change when the folks discover that the student is an attractive blonde.

This episode tells the unusual tale of Hooterville's founding. As the town prepares for its centennial, Oliver announces a reenactment of the town's origins and casts himself and Lisa in the roles of Horace and Doris Hooter.

When a blue feather arrives in the mail for Lisa, her Hungarian roots tell her that trouble is brewing. The feather is a symbol of malfortune to come, and she suspects it was sent by Hungarian gypsies, a warning that they are out to get her.

Don't count chickens before they hatch! Oliver thinks he's laid a gold egg of an idea when he decides to dive beak first into the business of raising chickens. Lisa, on the other hand, sees little difference between raising chickens and children.

All that glitters is not frosted cereal. After a jewelry heist in Chicago, the robbers foolishly stash their booty in the grain bin of a cereal manufacturer. Oliver and Lisa discover the jewels in their bowl of Crickly Wickly!

Oliver Wendell Douglas returns from farm to firm... law firm, that is. When a young and ambitious local graduates from law school, he looks for a potential partner in Hooterville. Oliver is the logical choice. Lisa and Eb help the new venture.

After partnering with a young, local lawyer, Oliver has opened a new law office in Hooterville. However, their secretary, Lisa, shows a lack of necessary skills. Soon, Lisa's job is on the line, even if she is married to one of the partners.

When the Young Peoples Agricultural Society holds their annual convention in Washington, D.C., local members Eb, Mr. Kimball, and Arnold the pig get ready to make the big trip. Oliver and Lisa serve as unintended chaperones.

While Lisa and Oliver consider what to do on their unplanned trip to Washington D.C., Mr. Haney rents their house to a family of eight. Meanwhile in the nation's capital, Lisa and Eb tour the White House, and Mr. Kimball makes official trouble.

When a charmingly sweet doe wanders onto the Douglas farm, an enchanted Lisa befriends the beautiful animal. Having had her heart won over, Lisa resolves to have all deer hunting banned in Hooterville, winning support however necessary.

Farmhand Eb plans to take his girlfriend to a fancy restaurant for her birthday. Only problem is he can't afford it. Oliver encourages Eb to get creative and figure out how to earn the money himself. And if Eb is anything, it's creative.

Lisa becomes enchanted with the diary of a Lydia Plunkett. Found in an old trunk in the barn, the diary from 1898 tells Lydia's life story as a successful businesswoman. Eb and Lisa are glued to every page of the story, but Oliver isn't impressed.

Mr. Haney and Fred Ziffel try to persuade Oliver to invest in a new business venture. "Looney Luke" Needlinger claim to have invented a machine that can turn hay into fresh milk. Oliver is skeptical and tries to prove the machine is a white lie.

Lisa's "Mudder" pays a surprise visit to Lisa and Oliver. Eb good-naturedly introduces her as the Queen of Sicily. As a result, the entire town treats her like royalty. They even go so far as to hold a special day in her honor.

Arnold Ziffel, Hooterville's beloved swine is thought to have rightful claim to a $20,000 fortune. The Birnbacher pork empire has promised that the descendant of the famous weather-predicting pig, Herman, will inherit the vast sum.

Oliver, Lisa and Eb travel to Chicago with Arnold to prove the pig is the rightful heir to the Birnbacher pork empire. Will this pig get rich? Arnold makes a surprising prediction that baffles all, including all the lawyers involved.

When Oliver returns home with Arnold, the citizens in town hold a large reception for Arnold. But when Oliver receives a phone call from a lawyer representing an eccentric relative of the Birnbachers, the riches go into question.

Oliver is mad over the town's dirt road, especially when he finds out that the state set aside money over thirty years ago to fix it. Oliver goes to the Capitol to get the road paved but hits a roadblock when the Ziffels' house must be torn down.

Lisa foretells of a mysterious stranger that will appear into Oliver's life. Enter Tadpole Talbot, Eb's childhood friend who has become a singing sensation. Tadpole has convinced Eb to go out on the road with him and join his band as a roadie.

Oliver become alarmed that the youth of his beloved town, Hooterville is dwindling so he calls an emergency town meeting to prevent them from leaving. The next thing Oliver knows is that his barn has been volunteered for the new youth center.

Oliver is asked to speak at the local high school about his illustrious law career and makes quite an impression on student Kathy Baxter. Oliver must contend with Kathy's fawning as well as her jealous boyfriend is not very happy with Oliver.

Hank Kimball proposes marriage to lady carpenter Ralph Monroe while under the influence of heavy medication. Lisa plans an amazing country wedding only to find out that, Sam, the Justice of the Peace, has forgotten to new his license.

Oliver plants his crops, worrying that they haven't been planted in time for a harvest. Lisa tries to be helpful and mixes up a batch of sour lemonade. Oliver pours out the bitter elixir in the newly planted field, with an unimaginable consequence.

Sam Drucker does not stock any cosmetics in his store, much to the chagrin of Lisa. Lisa decides to set up a "small" display in the store. When the merchandise is delivered, it forces Mr. Drucker to retreat to the front porch.

Mr. Haney discovers an old wish book dating back to 1898 that tells the story of Calvin and Tessie Whittaker who once owned the Douglases' farm and how Calvin traveled to Hollywood to pitch his idea of putting a mouse named Dickey into films.

Oliver and Lisa discover a root cellar under their house and become trapped when it collapses in on them. Their only hope to get rescued rides on a hilarious game of charades between Arnold the pig and Mr. Drucker.

Oliver goes to New York to finish up a case at his old firm. Meanwhile back on the farm, Lisa and Eb find a puppy left on the doorstep. Lisa, in all her innocence, leads Oliver to believe the puppy, affectionally named Freddie, is a human baby.

Oliver has been invited to give a speech at the Bar Association. He is there to advocate for the hiring of ex-convicts. He eventually ends up regretting his speech when he is forced to hire an ex-convict by the name of Willie Dunhill.

Oliver's crops are getting stomped on by Irene the cow. In his frustration, he fires a shotgun to scare Irene away. Instead the blast leads to a hilarious misunderstanding among Lisa, Eb and a life-sized fiberglass cow.

Oliver has become the new School Board President. Unfortunately, Oliver's first day on the job is anything but smooth. Arnold the pig is expelled from his duties as the school's mascot, and Fred Ziffel implores Oliver to defend Arnold.

After receiving a tax refund from the IRS, Oliver inspires his fellow citizens to make similar requests. There's only one problem... those making requests haven't paid their taxes! Nevertheless, the IRS mistakenly sends out half a million dollars!

Oliver is insistent that he and Lisa have a romantic Sunday afternoon picnic, all alone. His romantic gesture for two turns into a picnic for the entire town. Finally, Oliver finds them a romantic refuge in a most unlikely place.

Local boy Dinky Watson has one heck of a story to tell anyone who will listen. When Dinky convinces Lisa to buy a "moon rock" for the considerable sum of $14, Oliver suspects that she is the victim of a practical joke.

When Lisa's Uncle Fedor comes to visit her at the farm, he is visibly upset. He claims that someone is following him. Indeed, Fedor is convinced that the Secret Police are out to steal back a valuable scientific formula, which only he knows.

When Eb places an ad in a magazine claiming to be a wealthy landowner, it catches the eye of a young socialite. When the young woman makes an unexpected visit to Hooterville, Eb is forced to keep up his ruse.

Oliver is upset when he finds out Arnold the pig and he share the same birthday. Jealous that Arnold is getting more attention than he is, Oliver becomes convinced that Lisa is throwing him a surprise party and drives all over town in search for it.

Oliver and Lisa play host to four children from the city, who find themselves in Hooterville as part of a rural exposure program. The kids learn how to milk the cow, pick vegetables, plant seeds, and share sleeping quarters with four-legged friends.

Little Lori Baker, who after coming to stay with the Douglases on a rural experience program, is staying on at the Douglas farm. This city girl, like Oliver, has found that she loves the country life! Lisa decides to throw Lori a welcome party.

Lisa tells a rather fanciful version of how she met and fell in love with Oliver. The Douglases' house guest, little Lori Baker from the city, is all ears. The tale begins with how Lisa's father, the king, was exiled, causing Lisa to flee to Paris.

The residents of Hooterville assume that Oliver Douglas must be broke when Lisa is spotted looking for work and standing in line at the soup kitchen. But assumptions in this town, even logical ones, are bound to be wrong.

There is the old adage that warns never to discuss politics with your spouse... but what if you are both running for the same office?! That predicament comes true when Oliver and Lisa face each other in the Hooterville mayoral election.

Glenn Saxon, aka El Desperado, seeks justice for Mexicans and vengeance for his family. Orphaned by bandits, he targets the five men responsible, including outlaw Blackie Stark and Judge Wilkins. Amid schemes to control a wealthy daughter’s marriage, El Desperado maneuvers to make the guilty pay.
Clayton's sister is raped and murdered. Time for lethal revenge!
Shango is a Texas Ranger who finds himself up against a former Confederate officer and his gang of thugs who have been terrorizing a local border town in search of gold.

The Walker brothers took different paths—one an outlaw, one a Marshal, one a rancher. Yet they share one goal: avenging their father’s murder. When they finally find the killer, their clashing ideals lead to a deadly showdown.

In San Felipe, bandits target gold meant for the railroad - until a decoy chest thwarts them. When newcomers arrive, a masked gunman begins sabotaging the outlaws. But the real mastermind may be the town’s respected leader, hiding treachery behind wealth and charm.

programmes.t: I Am Sartana, Trade Your Guns for a Coffin
programmes.d: Sartana, a bounty hunter and gunfighter, witnesses a gold robbery and arrives in a suspicious town run by Samuel Spencer. Hired to protect the next shipment, Sartana fends off numerous incompetent villains, surviving their attempts on his life. Meanwhile, his nemesis, Sabbath—known for his white coat and parasol—arrives in town. With tensions rising, Sartana and Sabbath are headed for a final showdown to settle the score.

programmes.t: If You Want to Live... Shoot!
programmes.d: Johnny Dark returns from his gold mine and lands in a deadly crooked card game. Framed and hunted by bounty killer Stack, he’s wounded and taken in by the McGovern family - only to be caught in their land war against a ruthless railroad agent. As loyalties shift, Johnny’s past and fate collide.
A double-cross in an arms deal prompts Mexican revolutionary Pancho Villa to raid a US Army weapons depot in Columbus, New Mexico.

After a gang kills Apaches to steal their horses, Winnetou and his sister join forces with trapper Old Firehand. In the border town of Miramonte, they help defend the townspeople against the gang’s planned attack. As danger grows, Old Firehand also faces unexpected revelations about his former love and a long-hidden family secret.

Outlaws attack a band of settlers and kill everyone except a pregnant woman who's rescued by a band of Indians. The woman dies giving birth but Chief White Bear adopts her male baby, naming him "Shining Sky," and raising him as brother to his own son, Black Wolf.

The commander of a Texan fort in the Civil War refuses to surrender to the Northerners, and tries to buy the local Indian tribe chief's daughter. The sage man refuses, and the Southerners massacre the tribe and abduct the young squaw anyway. The noble squaw manages to escape, and hides out with a rough rancher, who dislikes Indians, but hates the Southerners more. The odd couple joins forces, and tactics, to exert ultimate vengeance on the men at the fort.

In early 20th-century Mexico, the guerrilla leader Tepepa is saved from execution by Doctor Price, an Englishman. Tepepa, a hero of the Revolution, is curious about the doctor’s motives. The chilling answer: to kill him himself. A deadly game of cat and mouse begins between Tepepa and the ruthless police chief, Cascorro.
A self-proclaimed Russian prince, a Mexican bandit and a radical Irish female journalist team up during the Mexican Revolution to find fortune and notoriety.

Captain O’Hara saves Mary from Navajo warriors and brings her safely to Fort San Antonio. But her fiancé, Major Brooks, is not only O’Hara’s rival but also a ruthless enemy of the Native tribes. As tensions rise, O’Hara must fight for peace while facing personal betrayal and growing conflict.

Agent Joe Ford, nicknamed “Dynamite Joe” for his explosive methods, is assigned to escort a vital gold shipment after a string of deadly ambushes threatens U.S. finances. With danger at every turn, Joe’s skills and dynamite are the last hope to stop the outlaws behind the attacks.

Little Rita is a female gunslinger who travels to the Far West chasing outlaws. She takes gold from them and hides it in a cave which she plans to blow up one day and get rid of the root of all evil: money.
Good Samaritan drifter, Benny Hudson and a stranded woman, Jenny finds themselves being torture; when they accidentally walk into an gang's hideout in a ghost town.
Ramon's parents are killed by men of landowner John Barrett. While trying to get revenge, Ramon is wounded but has saved the life of Rezza, an old disillusioned killer.

programmes.t: Dig Your Grave Friend... Sabata's Coming
programmes.d: Steve McGowan returns from war to avenge his father’s murder by a ruthless landowner. Imprisoned, he escapes with a bandit and steals a stagecoach—only to find the villain’s fiancée inside. As hired guns close in, alliances shift, and the fight for justice takes an unexpected turn.

In 1860s Mexico, General Ramirez hires American gunfighter Hallelujah to recover a stolen Aztec statue to win indigenous support. But a Scottish adventurer, feuding brothers, bandits, and the army are also in pursuit, turning the hunt into a chaotic race for power.

Sartana has a bounty on his head and he's wanted dead or alive. To eliminate this he makes a deal with the local politicians. If he hunts down the marauding Randal Brothers, the bounty will be removed.
Two brothers who hate each other are going to spend Christmas with their mother. She tries to get them together.

programmes.t: Shoot the Living and Pray for the Dead
programmes.d: After Dan Hogan and his gang rob a bank, they hire a mysterious man to guide them across the Mexican border in return for half of the loot.

Fists fly between Egypt and Briana and the battle lines are drawn! Twist and Sam go head-to-head. Romeo goes ballistic over the drama and enlists Eric to summon everyone to a sit down. Romeo's request enrages the Simmons family.

Romeo's sit-down sparks an uproar throughout the entire cast. Eric's caught in the crossfire and Angela puts Romeo on full blast. After Egypt battles Briana with her fists, she's forced to suffer the wrath of her mother Pepa.

Romeo's sit-down bursts into flames when he enters with Master P and his entourage. The Simmons family strikes back while Boogie stands up for battle. Later, Bow shows up and Romeo is pushed to the brink. Egypt enters the lion's den of Treach's fury.

Romeo quits the show and the cast responds. Treach finds out about Egypt's fist fight with Briana and there is hell to pay. Vanessa's battle with her weight reaches a breaking point when Angela pushes her to model for a swimwear photo shoot.

All hell breaks loose when a brawl explodes between Twist and JoJo. Danger strikes when Angela's stalker sneaks back into the picture and threatens her safety. The Simmons sisters clash over Vanessa's weight loss battle.

JoJo and Twist's fight rages on and bursts into flames. Sam and Egypt threaten Tee Tee's life-changing moment. Angela hits Bow with the burning question about their relationship until Bow spills that he has a secret surprise.

Stevie J and his daughter Savannah and son Stevie Jr. turn up the heat. Pepa's birthday party breaks into chaos. Jojo and Sam nearly come to blows over unresolved beef. A family feud ignites between Tee Tee and Egypt. Jojo and Tanice face heartbreak.

Angela's fast-moving relationship with her new boo raises alarm for Vanessa who has yet to meet him. Pepa comes to Sam's defense and faces off with Twist. Tee Tee stands by her controversial choice to exclude the Peppers from her wedding guest list.

A shocking cheating rumor is exposed. Angela's new boo drops a bomb. Pepa and Tee Tee face off. Stevie J interrogates Savannah on how she's raking in serious cash. Uncle Luke's daughter Cree helps Jojo plan a surprise for Tanice.

Jojo and Tanice's anniversary party goes all the way left when Briana confronts Boogie about being a disloyal friend. Lil Twist and Cree clash. Vanessa presses Angela about meeting her new man. Savannah digs up dirt on Boogie before their first date.

Shocking rumors of infidelity run wild. Boogie's attempt at an intervention for Briana backfires, and the battle lines are drawn. Tee Tee presses Shawn to go to couple's counseling before their trip to the altar.

Angela breaks down in tears when her split with the boxer faces public scrutiny. Cree struggles to reconnect with her father Uncle Luke. Vanessa warns Tee Tee about the rumor spreading behind her back and all hell breaks loose.

Cree and her father Uncle Luke face off in a fiery reunion. The cheating rumor continues to wreak havoc upon Twist's party and Tee Tee's on the warpath. Savannah and Boogie's second uncovers their true feelings for one another.

Tee Tee and Shawn fire up the cheating rumor when their wedding plans derail. Treach checks Egypt and Sam about squashing the beef with Tee Tee and Jojo. Briana's party spirals into chaos when a fight breaks out between Savannah and Eric.

Stevie J puts Savannah in the hot seat for her spending. JoJo and Tanice decide to keep their pregnancy a secret. Tee Tee enlists the help of her mother Maureen to put a stop to the cheating rumor, and there's hell to pay.

After her breakup, Angela plans to bare it all in a sexy swimsuit calendar. Briana and Boogie's friendship comes to an ugly head. Jojo and Sam sit down to squash their beef, but Jojo's upcoming showcase is threatened when tempers flare.

A scandal involving Angela is exposed. The legends Pepa, Uncle Luke and Brat come together at the judge's panel for Jojo's showcase. Egypt's under pressure to perform solo for the first time without Sam. Treach steps in to heal the family.

Jojo's showcase ends in a melee between Tanice and Sakoya, Jojo Hailey's daughter who exposes Angela's past. For the first time in over a year, Egypt and Tee Tee come to a head and settle the score in an epic family reunion.

Treach lays down the law to Egypt when Sam's arrest spirals into danger. Twist breaks the news of a gun charge to Mack Maine. Angela's abrupt move to Atlanta leads to an explosive girl's night. JoJo and Tanice's struggles nearly shut cameras down.

All hell breaks loose at a party when a beef erupts, and fists fly. Twist faces gun charges in court. Cree visits Angela's new home in Atlanta and reveals a heartbreaking secret. Tee Tee and Shawn clash over wedding rings in their rush to the altar.

Pepa warns Sam to be cautious when he breaks the news that he may be facing some serious jail time. Tee Tee's wedding planning rushes on, but will Pepa and Egypt make the guestlist? Uncle Luke advises Cree on squashing the beef with Sakoya.

Stevie J. confronts Savannah about squashing the beef with Tiny's daughter Sakoya. Tyran struggles to reunite Pepa and Tee Tee before the wedding. YDB steps onto the scene when JoJo gets the guys get together for some off-road action.

A surprise bachelor and bachelorette party for Tee Tee and Shawn ends in disaster. Treach supports Egypt's music career while Sam faces serious prison time. Eric and Layzie visit Eazy-E's gravesite, but rumors around his death must be put to rest.

JoJo and Tanice find themselves in a marriage crisis when JoJo's stood up on a group date. Tee Tee and Shawn's wedding plans spiral out of control. Sam seeks guidance from Layzie. Danger strikes for Briana when police come knocking at her door.

Briana's arrest spirals into a traumatic breakdown. Egypt's family crisis leads her to reach out to Tee Tee. Twist is under Young Money pressure when he returns to the stage for a big performance. JoJo and Tanice's marriage struggle gets real.

Between Covid, financial issues, a rainstorm and Pep not being invited, Tee Tee and Shawn's wedding falls apart. JoJo and Tanice are rocked by challenges of married life. Eric confronts Layzie Bone about his involvement in the Eazy-E Documentary.

Tee Tee's wedding day spirals into chaos, but a surprise from Pep shocks all. Meanwhile, Treach warns Sam that a dangerous future lies ahead and enforces protection over Egypt. Jojo plans something special for Tanice to keep the marriage lit.

Tee Tee and Maureen confront Pep about Egypt. Briana's new fling shocks all and brings her face to face with Pep at a family party. JoJo fights to save his marriage with a big surprise for Tanice. Eric spills the tea on his past with Tee Tee.
Angela plans for baby number two and visits a fertility doctor. Tee Tee and Egypt's rivalry comes to an unexpected head. Egypt rushes to marry her fiancé Sam even though Sam faces serious jail time.

Egypt and Sam rush to the little white chapel, but when they drop the bomb on Pep and Treach, Pep objects! Tanice and Sakoya's feud comes to a head. Eazy-E's celebration pushes the group to come together in peace and settle their differences.

The 50th anniversary of Hip Hop brings Bone Thugs-n-Harmony, Treach, and Kurupt onto one stage. A new baby is coming, but not everyone thinks it's good news. Meanwhile, a long-held secret romance is exposed, and an old rival makes a dramatic return.

Cree confronts Briana over fiery sneak disses on social media; Sakoya suspects her Mom is not being honest and discovers a troubling secret. Tyran offers Sam support as he deals with the aftermath of meeting Treach. Twist finds himself a new crush.

A pregnant Egypt goes on tour with Pepa, while Sam stays home alone. Jojo returns to music, and asks Eric to collaborate on a song. Aaliyah and Eric clash over Eric's gambling habit. Tiny and Sakoya have an explosive argument over Tiny's love life.

TT and Shawn clash over their new life in LA, Vanessa gets liposuction, and Cree and Briana finally faceoff over Briana's fiery sneak disses. Meanwhile, Twist plays peacemaker, and Layzie surprises Sakoya by showing up to her skate party uninvited.

Sam switches careers from rapper to food truck owner. Cree and Briana have an explosive confrontation at Briana's party. JoJo makes an offer on a house in Los Angeles, but keeps it a secret from Tanice.

Tee Tee decides to bury the hatchet when she learns that Egypt is pregnant. Twist turns to God to resist temptation, and tries to find his way back to an old flame. Aaliyah has had enough with Eric's gambling, and decides to do something about it.

Jojo confronts Buck over his toxic behavior; Sakoya attempts to mend her relationship with Tiny. Egypt and Sam decide who will be invited to their wedding. Treach suspects Sam has ulterior motives for marrying Egypt. Layzie mourns his Mother.

Romeo says he's changed & wants to apologize, but will his apology be accepted? Sam's case goes to court, and he gets news he didn't want to hear. Eric and Aaliyah finally discuss their issues, and Tanice and her dad clash over throwing ice at Jojo.

Romeo wants to apologize to Angela and Jojo, but they're hesitant to meet with him. Egypt continues to plan her wedding amid Sam's court case and unanswered RSVPs. Angela performs for the first time, but will her nerves get the best of her?

Romeo & Angela talk for the first time in years, but can their relationship be healed? Sam & Egypt celebrate their second wedding ceremony. To celebrate 50 years of Hip Hop, legends grace the stage, along with the cast, in an epic performance.

Bow Wow's arrest blows up in the tabloids and causes an uproar with Da Brat. R. Kelly's arrest ignites a buzzing child support battle with ex-wife Drea Kelly. Waka Flocka and wife Tammy Rivera put their wedding renewal vows to the ultimate test.

Bow faces tough love about his arrest and a dark cloud threatens to send him back to jail. Tammy's heart-to-heart with Drea Kelly sparks a revelation about her marriage to Waka. Deb's godson Brandon returns but bad blood isn't reconciled so easily.

A surprise visit from Angela Simmons rocks Bow's world! Tammy's insecurities threaten her first sexy music video. Ayana and Brandon face off and Waka questions Brandon's motives. Eazy-E's daughter seeks guidance from Deb and Brat.

Breaking news regarding R. Kelly's child support battle explodes into chaos. Deb and Brat clash over Drea Kelly. Ayana raises suspicions about Brandon firefighting; Bow and Brandon face off. ReeMarkable's performance backfires.

JD's throws a star-studded skate party including Usher and T-Boz. Snoop dishes out tough love on Bow. Brat blows up on LisaRaye when bankruptcy pushes her to a breaking point. Waka warns Deb that Brandon needs to steer clear of the family or else.

Bow enters dangerous territory when he meets a fiery new woman. ReeMarkable blows off her boyfriend and suffers the pay back. Deb has a family dinner to confront Brandon about a big fat lie. Waka reaches his boiling point and goes in for the kill.

Brandon's lies are exposed and that brings Brandon and Waka nearly to blows. Warning signs arise when Corri marks her territory with Bow. Brat questions ReeMarkable's intentions. Bow disses Drea Kelly right to her face.
Tammy goes ballistic when she catches Waka in a lie. Bow is blindsided when he learns of Corri's dangerous past. ReeMarkable disrespects Deb and Da Brat and battle lines are drawn.
